section: From Hidden Work to Shared Infrastructure
text:
From Hidden Work to Shared Infrastructure
A substantial amount of scholarly work takes place before research findings are produced. Researchers define constructs, design instruments, develop protocols, make methodological decisions, build tools, and create analytical frameworks. Yet much of this work remains hidden inside individual projects, appendices, supplementary files, or local research groups.
CATER is intended to help make this work more visible, reusable, and open to further development. This does not mean standardising the field around a single approach. Rather, it means creating better conditions for researchers to share the infrastructure they develop, learn from each other’s methodological decisions, and build stronger cumulative foundations for technology education research.






Local Scholarly Work
Constructs, instruments, protocols, tools, datasets, coding schemes, analytical frameworks, and methodological decisions developed within individual projects.










CATER Infrastructure Layer
A shared space for methods articles, open tools, training resources, working groups, textbooks, research clinics, and collaborative methodological development.










Field-Level Reuse
Stronger studies, clearer constructs, reusable resources, shared protocols, multi-site collaborations, and more credible technology education research.

title: CATER
text:
Why this matters
When methodological and conceptual work remains hidden, the field risks repeated reinvention, fragmented construct definitions, and inconsistent operationalisations of important ideas. CATER would provide a structure through which this work can be shared without requiring researchers to give up their own agendas, contexts, or theoretical commitments.

title: CATER
text:
Our Core Agendas


01. Infrastructure


Building the Foundation
Research in technology-education is only as good as its measurement. CATER focuses on the development of validated psychometric scales and open-source methodological tools.




02. Translation


From Data to Action
We believe that research is incomplete until it is accessible. Our translation wing develops teacher-ready toolkits and provides evidence-based briefings for policy stakeholders.




03. Accelerator


The CATER Network
Inspired by large-scale collaborative models, our Accelerator supports rapid, multi-site data collection. By pooling resources and expertise, our members can execute high-powered studies.

Explore the Concept







The CATER model


CATER is designed as a distributed centre rather than a single local research group. Its purpose is to connect researchers, support methodological development, and create shared infrastructure that strengthens research activity across existing institutions, groups, and projects.












Infrastructure
Developing shared tools, protocols, datasets, and validated instruments that technology education researchers can adapt, reuse, and build upon.







Translation
Turning research evidence into usable resources for teachers, teacher educators, curriculum designers, policymakers, and the wider technology education community.







Accelerator
Creating the conditions for multi-site studies, big-team science, shared grant applications, and collaborative research programmes across institutions.







Training
Supporting methodological capability through online seminars, workshops, research clinics, and an annual CATER unconference.










Future Impact Areas

Building Capacity Across Technology Education Research


CATER will track its contribution through the growth of its network, training activity, collaborative grant development, open research infrastructure, and research outputs.
